target.title: fix(media): parse local file extensions across path styles
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105439.

`getFileExtension()` parsed non-URL local paths with host-native `path.extname()`. On Linux/macOS, a Windows-style path with an extensionless filename under a dotted directory, such as `C:\\Folder.with.dot\\image`, was treated as if `.dot\\image` were the file extension.

## Why This Change Was Made

The media-core package already has `extnameFromAnyPath()`, which extracts the final filename segment using both POSIX and Windows basename semantics. Reusing it keeps local path parsing cross-platform while leaving the existing HTTP URL parsing branch unchanged.

## User Impact

Media MIME detection and plugin SDK consumers no longer get a corrupted extension for Windows-style local paths when OpenClaw runs on non-Windows hosts.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: After the fix, `getFileExtension()` treats both slash styles as path separators for local paths, so `C:\\Folder.with.dot\\image` has no extension instead of returning the corrupted `.dot\\image` value, while normal Windows filenames such as `C:\\media.folder\\clip.MP4` still return `.mp4`.
Real environment tested: Repository `openclaw/openclaw`, branch `fix/path-extension-windows-105439`, commit `e4859a90fff851d52b90d3b1b30307d144ec1ae4`, using a git worktree at `/datad/github/openclaw-issue105439` on Linux with Node `v24.14.1` and pnpm `11.2.2`.
Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```shell
node - <<'NODE'
const path = require('node:path');
const input = String.raw`C:\\Folder.with.dot\\image`;
console.log('input:', input);
console.log('native path.extname on this host:', JSON.stringify(path.extname(input)));
function basenameFromAnyPath(value) { return path.win32.basename(path.posix.basename(value)); }
function extnameFromAnyPath(value) { return path.extname(basenameFromAnyPath(value)); }
console.log('fixed cross-path extname:', JSON.stringify(extnameFromAnyPath(input)));
NODE
git diff --check
pnpm exec oxlint packages/media-core/src/mime.ts packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:core:test
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false pnpm check:changed -- packages/media-core/src/mime.ts packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts
```
Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the verification:
```
input: C:\Folder.with.dot\image
native path.extname on this host: ".dot\\image"
fixed cross-path extname: ""
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
✓ unit-fast packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts (121 tests) 240ms
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 121 passed (121)
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
[check:changed] lanes=core, coreTests
[check:changed] typecheck core
[check:changed] typecheck core tests
[check:changed] lint core changed files
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Database-first legacy-store guard passed.
runtime-sidecar-loaders: local runtime sidecar loaders look OK.
Import cycle check: 0 runtime value cycle(s).
Process exited with code 0.
```
Observed result after fix: The cross-path extension helper returns an empty extension for an extensionless Windows basename under a dotted directory, and the regression test suite passes with the new Windows-style coverage.
What was not tested: Full `pnpm build`, full `pnpm test`, live media downloads, and Windows-native runtime were not run; this patch is limited to shared path parsing and focused media-core validation plus `check:changed`.

## Test Plan

- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm exec oxlint packages/media-core/src/mime.ts packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false pnpm check:changed -- packages/media-core/src/mime.ts packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts`

## Risk

Low. The change replaces host-native extension parsing only for plain local paths with an existing media-core helper that already normalizes POSIX and Windows final filename segments. The HTTP URL branch is unchanged.
